corrections.correction: UNESCO's broad Chaco center phase, Bonito building phase, regional network duration and later residential reuse are distinct scopes; keep their dates separate.
Brown2013 argues sustained occupation/growth through the mid-1100s drought rather than immediate abandonment followed by Mesa Verde replacement.
Lentz2021 woodland-impact interpretation must be shown beside Wills2014 contrary evaluation; neither citation count nor recency alone settles a causal collapse claim.
~2414 BCE maize pollen is a cited previous finding in Lentz; it does not date intensive farming or village formation. Supplied bean onset not imported without context review.
Plog/Heitman2010 supports early mortuary differentiation; a matrilineal dynasty requires the separate 2017 human-DNA source and relevant descendant/community context.
Kemp2017 sampled dogs/turkeys, not humans. Migrating households are inferred from animal patterns; do not label it human genomic ancestry or map a precise route.
The 2025 primary study gives approximately 1275–1400 from ceramics; the supplied 1280–1540s conflates a broader Rio Grande chronology with this community.
Southern US–Mexico borderlands are geographically distinct from the northern US Four Corners. Selective cultural adoption and trade are not proof of direct north-to-south migration.
Documented road segments, symbolic alignments and interaction networks do not establish continuous historical travel routes.
Local farming-community departure does not mean Pueblo peoples disappeared, nor does a source about Pueblo migration establish the first Navajo presence.
Room 28 burning is interpreted as probable ritual closure; do not recast it as a documented conflict event. No unsourced regional warfare layer added.
